content:
The image shows soybean seeds held in a hand. Key observations:

- Seeds are mostly tan/cream colored (normal soybean color)
- Several seeds show distinct purple to dark purple blotches and spots on the seed coat
- The purple discoloration varies from small specks to large blotches covering a significant portion of the seed surface
- Some seeds appear entirely purple/dark on one side
- The discoloration pattern extends from the hilum area on some seeds

This is a classic presentation of **Purple Seed Stain** caused by *Cercospora kikuchii*. The pink-to-purple discoloration on seed coats, ranging from specks to large blotches, is the defining feature. This matches the symptom description exactly: "Pink to purple seed discoloration extending from the hilum."

While Cercospora (leaf blight phase) is a related class, the image shows seeds, not leaves — and Purple_Seed_Stain specifically describes this seed coat symptom.
